questions.text: What enables a Chameleon-style autoregressive decoder to predict both text and image content?

options.A: A shared token-ID vocabulary containing text tokens, discrete image codes, and separators.
options.B: A text-only output vocabulary with image patches used only as continuous input features.
options.C: A frozen vision encoder that converts every output word into an image caption.
options.D: A separate diffusion model that replaces next-token prediction for every modality.

questions.explanation: Discrete image codes and text IDs occupy one vocabulary, allowing a single autoregressive output distribution to predict either modality. An image decoder renders the generated image codes.

questions.text: Your image tokenizer loses fine text detail even when decoding the correct image codes. What follows for generation through that tokenizer?

options.A: A larger text vocabulary automatically restores the missing pixel detail.
options.B: Longer captions guarantee exact reconstruction of the original image.
options.C: Better next-token prediction alone cannot remove that reconstruction bottleneck.
options.D: Removing image separators makes the quantizer lossless.

questions.explanation: A lossy tokenizer constrains the information available to its decoder. Improving code prediction alone cannot recover detail that the representation discards.

questions.text: quantize_patch returns best + IMG_OFFSET, where IMG_OFFSET=32. If nearest-codebook lookup selects index 5, which shared-vocabulary ID is returned?
questions.explanation: Image code indices are offset past the 32 text IDs: 5+32=37.
